correctness.rationale: The weight distribution follows from Kwiatkowski Proposition 4.2 with m=1,l=0; the two nonzero weights (q-1)q^(k-1)(q^k-1) and (q-1)q^(k-1)(q^k-2) have frequencies 2(q^k-1) and (q^k-1)^2, giving full q^(2k) words and rank 2k. The first k Griesmer terms sum to q^(2k)-3q^k+2 and the remaining k ceilings to q^k-2 by the exact floor at j=0; G=N-1. The integer-ceiling increment for d+1 is 1 at every q^i dividing d, giving k increments for q>2 and k+1 for q=2. Independently verified 70 prime-power (q,k) arithmetic pairs and constructed the exact full weight distributions for (q,k)=(2,2),(3,2) from the generator columns. Checks are corroborative, proof all parameters algebraic. Griesmer applies only to q-ary linear codes.

value.rationale: Equal-dimension coupling is the canonical omitted parameter boundary of the published construction. Determining its exact defect AND excluding larger distance for all q and k resolves the natural parameterwise optimal-distance question, useful for selecting and benchmarking two-weight linear codes. It is more than a finite table or a trivial parameter renaming, though not a new universal coding bound.

final_claim: For every prime power q and k>=2, the equal-dimension SR-sum of the q-ary length-q^k-1 simplex expansion has length N=(q^k-1)^2, dimension 2k, distance d=(q-1)q^(k-1)(q^k-2), Griesmer G_q(2k,d)=N-1; G_q(2k,d+1)-N equals k for q=2 and k-1 for q>2, so d is linear-distance optimal.
